_comment: Key anniversaries. When the slider year equals 'year', an event popup fires with the dual-narrative quote pair. Sources mirror the study library (02-sources/israelite-history.md).

events.title: The first 'Israel'
events.bible: The exodus generation — or so the tradition would say.
events.archaeology: The Merneptah Stele (c. 1208 BCE) names 'Israel' for the first time in any record — a people in the highlands of Canaan, already there, already named. No exodus, no conquest: a people emerging from within.

events.title: The collapse is complete
events.bible: The period of the judges — 'everyone did what was right in their own eyes.'
events.archaeology: The Bronze Age collapse (c. 1200-1150) empties the great cities and the Egyptian garrisons. The highland villages boom: this is where Israel actually forms.

events.title: David takes Jerusalem
events.bible: The City of David is conquered and becomes the capital of the United Monarchy (2 Sam 5).
events.archaeology: The archaeological Jerusalem of the 10th century: a small highland town of a few thousand, with no signs of empire. The Tel Dan Stele confirms the dynasty — not the empire.
events.source: 2 Samuel 5; Tel Dan Stele; Finkelstein & Silberman

events.title: The kingdom splits
events.bible: After Solomon, Rehoboam's harshness tears the kingdom in two (1 Kgs 12).
events.archaeology: Whether there was ever a united monarchy is debated (minimalists vs. maximalists); what is certain is that from the 9th century on, there are two states — and the north is the strong one.

events.title: Ahab at Qarqar
events.bible: The Bible's 'evil' king — who in Assyrian records commands 2,000 chariots.
events.archaeology: The Kurkh Monolith (853 BCE): 'Ahab the Israelite' contributes 2,000 chariots to the coalition that checks Assyria — the largest chariot force in the alliance. Biblical villain, regional power.

events.title: Jehu bows to Assyria
events.bible: Jehu, the reformer who wiped out the House of Omri (2 Kgs 9-10).
events.archaeology: The Black Obelisk (c. 825 BCE) shows Jehu — or his envoy — prostrate before Shalmaneser III, paying tribute. The earliest surviving image of an Israelite king: on his knees.

events.title: Samaria falls
events.bible: The northern kingdom ends; its people are deported and become the ten lost tribes (2 Kgs 17).
events.archaeology: Sargon II: 'I conquered Samaria and carried away 27,290 people.' The destruction layer is real. The north never returns.

events.title: Sennacherib at the gates
events.bible: The angel of the Lord strikes 185,000 Assyrians; Jerusalem is saved (2 Kgs 19:35).
events.archaeology: The Taylor Prism: 46 walled cities taken, Hezekiah 'shut up like a bird in a cage.' The Bible records the tribute it omits — and Jerusalem's survival is the part both sides share.

events.title: Nineveh falls
events.bible: Nahum's 'city of blood' gets what the prophets promised it.
events.archaeology: A coalition of Babylonians and Medes sacks the largest city on earth. The Assyrian empire ends in fire — leaving a power vacuum Josiah will run into.

events.title: Josiah dies at Megiddo
events.bible: The reformer-king marches out to block Pharaoh Necho — and is killed (2 Kgs 23:29).
events.archaeology: The biblical text says he died; archaeology says Megiddo was destroyed around 609. The two records finally agree — and the reform dies with him.

events.title: The first deportation
events.bible: Jehoiachin, the court, the craftsmen — ten thousand captives to Babylon (2 Kgs 24).
events.archaeology: The Babylonian Chronicle BM 21946 confirms the siege, the capture, and the appointment of a puppet king — 'in the month of Adar, on the second day.'

events.title: Jerusalem burns
events.bible: The temple of Yahweh, the dwelling of God on earth, is burned to the ground (2 Kgs 25).
events.archaeology: The destruction layer at Jerusalem is unmistakable. The Davidic monarchy ends after 400 years. The exiles carry the trauma east — and the pen with them.

events.title: Cyrus takes Babylon
events.bible: The Lord raises up Cyrus, 'his anointed,' and the exiles are told to go home (Isa 45:1; Ezra 1).
events.archaeology: The Cyrus Cylinder records the policy: return the peoples, restore the temples. The exile ends by imperial decree — and the scrolls come back changed.
